items.one_line: Answer to the SRAM2 question: yes, #48 already asks for exactly that move and gives both reasons (error correction and erase on tamper), #46 records it as a decision and #848 lists it as a choice to make. What none of them says is that SRAM2 is the non-secure bank today, so it is a bank swap, and that the stack must move too. Two comments (#48, #854); no new issue.

new_defects.quote: post-transfer assert `DIEPTSIZ.XFRSIZ` did not exceed declared length
new_defects.note: This threat-model row lists a post-transfer length assert as an existing mitigation. A search of every .rs file in the tree for DIEPTSIZ and XFRSIZ finds nothing, the driver dependency (synopsys-usb-otg 0.4.0) has no such check either, and the non-secure HID write reduces the result to is_ok() (nonsecure/src/usb/hid.rs:75). The report listed this claim as unchecked; it is documentation drift, not a code defect, and would fit the list in #866.
